Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround. Quick note to make the benchmark criteria explicit so we're aligned for the MAP:

Benchmark success criteria (proposed, we can adjust):
- Functional: top-1 accuracy / relevance >= your baseline on provided prompt set (we'll map metrics to each prompt).
- Latency targets: P50 / P95 / P99 measured on dedicated capacity; target P95 <= 250ms for 512-token responses, P95 <= 1200ms for 2048-token responses.
- Cost targets: amortized cost per 1k input+output tokens <= $8 (we'll provide cost breakdown across batching/quantization options).
- Stability: no >1% failure rate (timeouts or OOM) across benchmark runs.

Model shortlist (finalize with you):
- Llama-2-70b-chat (8-bit quantized) — strong for instruction-following, good latency on our dedicated pools.
- Mistral-Instruct-7B — low-cost option with good latency; may require prompt engineering for edge cases.
- Redwood-Alpha-8B (our Redwood-verified medium model) — good tradeoff of quality and cost.
- OpenChat-13B — for tasks where instruction-following precision is critical; higher latency/cost.

Responsibilities:
- Redwood (Marissa / Camila / Mateo): run benchmarks, provide latency+cost report, recommend model and quantization profile.
- Acme (Samantha / Priya): supply labeled sample prompts, success labels where available, and confirm SLOs.
- Acme Security (Tom): confirm access approach and provide SOC2 artifacts or a list of required evidence.

We'll upload a revised MAP and the benchmarking runbook to the HubSpot deal and Drive folder (link below) after we confirm dataset delivery.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-map
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2027-0112

If that plan looks good I'll: (1) update the MAP spreadsheet with the responsibilities and dates, (2) schedule the benchmarking slot with infra for 6/24, and (3) send a calendar invite to the group.

-Marissa
